title: Family Album
subtitle: How to use it. In very plain words.

intro.text: This is our family's photo album. It lives on our own computer, not on anybody else's. Nothing in it is for sale, and nobody sees it unless we send it to them.
**The one thing to remember:** you cannot break it. Nothing you press deletes a photograph for good. If something looks wrong, say so — it can be put back.

blocks.text: There is no password to remember. That is on purpose — passwords get forgotten, written on paper, and reused.

items: Go to the album's web address. Somebody in the family will have sent it to you.
Type your email address and press the button.
Look in your email. There will be a message with a link in it.
Press that link. You are in.

blocks.text: The link only works once, and only for about fifteen minutes. That is what keeps it safe. If you take too long, just ask for another one.

**No email arrived?** Only people the family has invited can get in, so the album will not send a link to an address it does not know. Ask whoever runs the album to invite you. Also look in your junk folder.
Once you are in, it remembers you on that phone or computer for a few months. You will not have to do this often.

Open a trip and you land on its **timeline**: the days it happened, in order, top to bottom. That is how people remember a holiday — the day we got there, the day of the boat, the last morning — so that is what the album shows first.
On a computer

Down the left there is a list of every day, with how many photographs it holds and that day's walks and outings under it. Press a day, or an outing, to jump to it. The day you are looking at is marked as you scroll.
On a phone
There is no room for the list, so the date at the top of the screen does the job. Press the date and every day appears, with its outings under it; press one to go there.
Press any photograph to see it big. Press it again to see it at full size. The arrow keys, or a swipe, move to the next one.
Keeping the ones you love

Every photograph has a heart. Press **Add to favorites** while you are looking at it big, or the ♡ on its little square in a grid. To find them again, press **Favorites** in the menu for every favorite in the album, or the **Favorites** tab on a trip or a collection for just that one. **Mine** is the ones you marked, newest first; **Everyone's** is the whole family's, with the ones most of us marked at the top.
Other ways to look

rows: Timeline
The days, in order. This is the usual way.
Map

Where photographs were taken. Useful for “where was that beach?” Use **Color by** to ring each photograph in the color of its day, its outing or the person who added it. Days go from dark purple on the first day to yellow on the last.
Activities
The walks, rides and outings, with how far and how long.
Photos
All of them in a plain grid, newest first.
Overview
A few numbers and a handful of photographs picked at random.

blocks.text: Every timeline, every map and every grid has a search box. Type a word or two and press **Search**.

The good part: it does not send you to a separate list of results. It narrows the page you are already on. So the photograph you were after comes back still sitting under the day it was taken, with that day around it.
What to type

items: What is in it: _lobster_, _cake_, _lighthouse_, _snow_
What was happening: _birthday_, _hiking_, _christmas_
Something written in the picture: a banner, a sign, writing on the back of an old print
A name somebody typed in the notes

blocks.text: More ways to narrow
Under the search box there is **More ways to narrow**. Press it and you can also ask for:

rows: Uploaded by
Who put it into the album. Usually, but not always, who took it.
Who is in it
A person or a pet. Choose two names and you get the ones they are _both_ in.
Part of the trip
Only photographs from one walk or outing.
Year
Only that year.
Type
Photographs, video clips, YouTube links, or 3D scans.

blocks.text: A narrowed page has its own web address. You can save it, or send it to somebody else in the family, and they see the same thing.

items: Press **Upload** in the menu at the top.
Choose the photographs, or drag them onto the page.
Wait. Each one says when it is done.

blocks.text: Big ones take a few seconds each. You can send up to 200 at a time. Once they have all gone up, the album takes a few more minutes to finish them, two at a time — that part happens on the album's own computer, so it carries on even if you close the page or your phone goes to sleep.
If an upload stops partway

The connection drops, the phone goes to sleep, the page gets closed: whatever the reason, the fix is the same. **Choose all the same photographs again and upload them again.** There is no need to work out which ones made it.

**Nothing gets doubled.** The album recognizes a photograph it already has and does not add it a second time. If you chose a trip, an outing or a collection to upload to, the one it already has is put there instead, and the page says so. Only the ones that were missing are added.

This works for the very same files. A copy that has since been edited, or saved again by another app, counts as a different photograph. A photograph somebody else added stays where they put it; only they or an admin can move it.
Where do they end up?
The album reads the date the camera wrote and puts each photograph on the trip that was happening then. If no trip matches, it waits in **Photos without a trip** until somebody files it.
Straight into an outing or a collection

Open the outing and press **Add photos to this activity**, or open the collection and press **Upload photos to this collection**, then choose the photographs. They go there whatever their dates say. Ones put in a collection also go onto a trip if their dates match one, since a collection is a scrapbook, not a place.

**Photographs from an Android phone often arrive with no place on them.** That is the phone, not the album: it removes the location from the copy it hands over. The map can still be filled in afterwards — see “Fixing something that is wrong”.
Three words the album uses. They are simpler than they sound.

rows: Trip
A stretch of days in one place. A photograph is on one trip, or none.
A holiday
Collection
A gathering of photographs from anywhere, for any reason. A photograph can be in many.
A scrapbook
Activity
One outing inside a trip: a walk, a ride, a paddle, an afternoon.
A day out

blocks.text: Activities: why the distances are there

If somebody imported a trace from a watch or a phone, the outing knows how far it went, how long it took and how much climbing there was. The photographs taken during those hours are gathered onto it by themselves.

Sometimes the album gets that wrong — two people did two different things that afternoon, and a clock cannot tell which. To fix it, open the outing, press **Select photos**, tick the ones that do not belong, and press **Take off this activity**. They stay on the trip, back under their own day. Nothing is deleted.
Who was on it

The album files a photograph by the date the camera wrote, and a date cannot tell two families apart: if a cousin uploads their own holiday from the same fortnight, it lands on your trip. Open the trip's **Settings**, or an outing's **Edit**, and tick who was there. From then on only their uploads are filed there by date. Ticking nobody means everyone, which is how every trip starts.
This only changes the album's own guesswork. Anything anybody puts on a trip or an outing by hand stays exactly where they put it, and what is already filed is left alone.
Saying what it was

A trip, a collection and an outing can each carry a few sentences about what it was. Open it and press **Add a description** — under the title on a trip or a collection, under the times on an outing — and write them. If the AI helper is switched on there is a second button beside Save: type what only you know — whose birthday it was, why you turned back, what ties these photographs together — and press **Write it around this**, and the helper writes the paragraph using what you said and a few of the photographs. What comes back lands in the same box, so you can change any of it before you save.
The album can keep track of who is in a photograph, so you can ask for “the ones with Mom in them”.
Two separate things, on purpose

rows: Tagging somebody
You point at a face and say who it is. Anyone who can edit the photograph can do this. It does not switch anything on.
Recognizing somebody
The album learns a face and looks for it in new photographs. This needs that person's agreement, and only an admin can turn it on.
Using a name in descriptions
The album may use the name when it writes about a photograph. Also their choice, also separate. Children are never named.

blocks.text: This is fussier than it needs to be for a family album, and that is deliberate: a face is not the same kind of thing as a caption, and somebody may be happy to be named without wanting to be recognized.
Pets work the same way, without the agreement — a dog cannot consent, and does not need to.
Everything in the album is private until you decide otherwise. There are three ways to let somebody outside the family see something.

rows: Private
Only the family. This is how everything starts.
A secret link
Anyone you send the link to. They do not need to sign in. Nobody else can find it.
Public
Anybody at all, including strangers who find it by chance.

blocks.text: You can share a whole trip, a collection, or just one outing. Press **Share**, and the link is there ready to copy. Paste it into a message and it carries the title and a picture with it.

**A link shows everything in that thing.** A shared trip shows all its photographs — and, if there are traces from a watch or phone, the paths they recorded. That is a record of where people were and when. Share an outing on its own if that is all you meant to send.
Changed your mind? Press **New link** and the old one stops working straight away, or **Stop sharing** to close it altogether.

sections.heading: Putting photographs on the map, from a phone

blocks.text: A photograph from a camera usually knows where it was taken. Scans don't, and neither do many photographs sent from phones, so the map has nowhere to put them. You can put them there yourself, on a phone or a computer: in the car after a day out, or at home afterwards.
Getting there

items: Open the trip.
Press **Map**.
Press **Place photos**, just under the map.

blocks.text: Placing
The top of the screen is the map. Underneath are your photographs, a day at a time. The map stays put while you scroll through them.

items: Tap every photograph taken in one spot. A tick appears on each. **Choose the day** ticks a whole day at once.

Get the map to the spot. Drag it with a finger and pinch to zoom, or type a town into **Find a town or landmark**. If you are standing there, press **Where I am** and the phone finds the spot for you.
Tap the spot. A pin appears. If it is not quite right, tap again.
Press **Put them here**. That's it. If you got it wrong, press **Undo** straight away.

blocks.text: **Not placed yet** shows only the photographs with no place, or only a guessed one. **All photos** shows everything, for moving one that is in the wrong spot. The search box and **More ways to narrow** work here the same as everywhere else.
Moving one that is in the wrong spot
Choose **All photos**. Tap the photograph in the list, or tap its pin on the map; a blue ring goes round it. Then tap where it should be and press **Put them here**.
**Lines on the map are your walks and drives.** If a photograph was taken on the walk, it was taken somewhere on that line, which makes the spot much easier to find.
**Only your own.** You can place the photographs you added. An admin can place anybody's.

rows: An upload stopped partway
Upload all the same photographs again. The ones the album already has are recognized and skipped, so nothing is doubled. See “Adding your own photographs”.
Wrong date, so it is under the wrong day

Open the photograph and change the date. On the timeline you can pick up a whole day at once — press **Select photos**, then **Select this day** — which is the usual fix for a box of old scans that all landed on the day somebody scanned them.
No place on the map

On the trip's map, press **Place photos**: tap the photographs, tap the spot, press **Put them here**. It works on a phone. See “Putting photographs on the map, from a phone”. For a single photograph you can also open it and use **Set a place**.
On the wrong outing
Open the outing, **Select photos**, **Take off this activity**. It stays on the trip.
On the wrong trip, or no trip
Select it in any grid and use the bulk actions to put it on the right one.
A photograph that should not be there
Press **Trash** and say why. It leaves the album at once but is not gone: an admin can put it back. Anyone in the family can do this.
The same photograph twice
If they are the very same file, the album already folded them into one. If they are two similar shots, trash the one you do not want.
A description that is wrong or unkind
Just edit it. What you write is yours and the album will not overwrite it.

sections.heading: What the computer writes by itself

blocks.text: The album can ask an AI helper to describe photographs, so they can be found by searching for what is in them. This is off unless somebody turned it on, and it is worth knowing what it does.

items: It writes a title, a caption, a description and a list of search words.
It is told the names of people the family has agreed to name. It is never told a child's name.
It never sees faces as faces: no face data of any kind is sent to it.
Anything you write yourself is left alone. It only replaces its own words.
A trip, a collection or a single photograph can be kept out of it entirely.

blocks.text: If a description says something you do not like, change it. Your words win.
The **Graph** page is a different trick: it draws photographs that look alike near each other. It is a good way to find the four nearly identical shots of the same puddle.

rows: Timeline
Photographs laid out by the day they were taken.
Trip
A stretch of days in one place.
Collection
A gathering of photographs chosen by hand.
Activity
One outing inside a trip.
Track
A path recorded by a watch or a phone.
Tag
Pointing at somebody in a photograph and saying who they are.
Trash
Out of the album, but not gone. An admin can put it back.
Member
Somebody in the family who can sign in.
Admin
A member who can also invite people and change the settings.
Share link
A secret web address that lets somebody see one thing without signing in.

blocks.text: Ask whoever set the album up. It is one of the family, not a company, and there is no support queue. Tell them what you pressed and what happened — that is usually enough to find it.
This guide covers using the album. Installing and running it is a different document, SETUP.pdf, and nobody needs it to look at photographs.
